text:
maya: Heads-up — during the canary for runtime-v2.3 I noticed /v1/generate returning 429s with inconsistent headers across instances. Some instances had Retry-After only, others included X-Route-Quota-Remaining and X-Route-Quota-Reset. Anyone else seen this?

devon: Yep saw a few in logs this morning, thought it was transient. Can you paste the raw headers you captured?

maya: Sure — two examples from the same minute:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Route-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Route-Quota-Reset: 1700001234
Content-Type: application/json
```

akshay: That looks like router fallback. Intended behavior: when per-route bucket is hit, runtime should emit route-specific headers (remaining, reset, bucket id). If we fallback to global capacity, we currently emit just Retry-After. Seems some nodes are hitting fallback path while others return proper route quota info.

tess: From the SDK side — do we expect clients to rely on X-Route-* headers or on Retry-After + body? We need a deterministic contract before we change SDK behavior.

samir: Short-term SDK guidance: treat Retry-After as authoritative for backcompat, but attempt to read new quota headers when present. Also, drop-in fallback: if headers missing, parse body for a quota_hint field if present. Example pseudo-js:
```js
const ra = parseInt(res.headers['retry-after']) || null;
const remaining = parseInt(res.headers['x-route-quota-remaining']);
if (Number.isNaN(remaining)) { remaining = res.body?.quota?.remaining ?? null; }
// then expose both to callers
```

devon: Server-side fix suggestion: always emit a short, normalized quota hint header that survives proxies. Some infra strips X-* headers. Maybe use Rate-Limit-Remaining / Rate-Limit-Reset (no leading X) or a standard-like header `Quota-Hint` that includes key=value pairs. Also include identical structured data in the 429 response body to make it SDK-friendly.

akshay: Good point about proxies. We already saw one customer infra strip `X-Route-*`. Plan: keep Retry-After for compatibility, add `RateLimit-Route-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Route-Reset` (no X), and include body: "{ \"quota\": { \"type\": \"route\", \"bucket\": \"<id>\", \"remaining\": 0, \"reset\": 1700001234 } }". We'll gate header emission behind a small canary flag and roll across nodes.

tess: For backwards compatibility in SDKs: implement linear fallback order — check RateLimit-Route-Remaining, then X-Route-Quota-Remaining, then body.quota. Also emit a deprecation warning if only old headers are present so we can track client versions.

maya: What's our rollout plan? We need to avoid oscillations where some nodes emit new headers and others don't, causing client confusion and flaky retry logic.

akshay: Roll plan proposal:
1) Add dual header emission in runtime (both X- and RateLimit- prefixed) behind feature flag.
2) Canary to 5% for 30m, monitor 429 header parity metric and client-side errors.
3) Expand to 25% for 2h, then 100% if parity > 99.5% and no increase in customer 429 spikes.
We'll also add a router instrumentation to tag whether response came from per-route bucket path vs global fallback.

samir: I'll update SDK PR to implement fallback logic + opt-in telemetry (which header seen). Will include unit tests with the two header shapes and body-only case.

deploy-bot: canary deploy: runtime-v2.3.1 -> cluster-canary at 1724010000 :rocket:

devon: I'll open runtime issue (RT-9482) to track the header parity bug and link the rollout plan. akshay can you own the feature-flag PR?

akshay: Yep, will send the runtime PR and add the router metric. Also will add an integration test that fakes a proxy stripping X-* headers to assert we still expose RateLimit- headers.

maya: Thanks — I'll add a short note to the runbook and ping support to watch customer dashboards. @tess please add SDK PR to the changelog and coordinate a minor release. :thumbsup:

tess: On it — will create PR referencing RT-9482 and include migration notes.

maya: Great. I'll close the loop after the 25% window and post metrics. Thanks everyone. :pray:
